newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil tax to avoid repeated investment charges.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax to avoid repeated investment charges.

text.p: A new Brazilian tax on financial transactions will be structured so as to avoid repeated charges on different steps involved in making investments in Brazil, Central Bank international affairs director Gustavo Franco said.

Investors would pay a 0.2 percent charge under the new Provisional Contribution on Financial Movements (CPMF) tax which takes effect from January 23 only when beginning and closing an investment operation in Brazil.
But they would not be charged on any movements of capital in between, Franco said.
"There would be an entry toll and an exit toll," Franco told reporters.
The final details of the new tax, aimed at raising funds for Brazil's ailing health service, are still being worked out.
Government officials and stock market analysts have voiced concern that the new tax may discourage national and foreign investment in stocks.
